messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: abnormal GPU queue growth in pool gpu-east-2 after rollout model-eta-v2.1. queue_length=4320, enqueued/sec=820 -> 4x baseline, p99_latency=6.2s, token_throttle_rate=18%. Autoscaler attempts failing: scale_request denied (quota limit). Runbook: https://runbooks/internal/gpu-queue

sara: paging @oncall @dan @ash — seeing a bunch of queued requests and 503 spikes. can someone take?

dan: on it. I'm looking at autoscaler logs, it tried to request +8 GPUs but cloud quota returned 403/quota_exceeded. Also seeing KV cache per-session mem jump after the v2.1 tokenizer change.

ash: taking pager. quick ask — is this new-traffic amplification (longer contexts) or an enqueue bug?

mike: customer-impact: several enterprise customers hitting degraded responses and intermittent 503s on /v1/generate. Error rate up from 0.3% -> 5.8% last 10m. Self-serve lessee traffic slowed but not fully blocked.

julia: suspect warmup behavior: model v2.1 starts with longer initial contexts (weird tokenizer chunking) causing kv-cache to grow per connection and keep sessions pinned to GPUs longer. that increases mem pressure -> less capacity for active inference -> enqueueing.

dan: confirming logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:03Z autoscaler: request_scale(pool=gpu-east-2, desired=40) -> denied (quota_limit)
2026-03-15T03:12:04Z autoscaler: scale_request_rejected reason=quota_limit current=34 quota=34
2026-03-15T03:12:05Z runtime: session_alloc: mem_per_session=360MB (baseline 120MB)
2026-03-15T03:12:06Z runtime: kv_cache_size per-session increased, avg_sessions_per_gpu=112
```

dan: also seeing burst of long-context requests during rollout traffic (batch of warmup calls from rollout canaries).

ash: mitigation options: 1) rollback to model-eta-v2.0, 2) route new traffic to smaller variant (model-eta-lite), 3) emergency increase quota (slow, cloud tickets), 4) temporary max_context cap at proxy to limit session mem.

sara: prioritize rollback + proxy cap. rollback sounds fastest. Julia, can we flip routing to v2.0 for critical routes?

julia: yes — can set routing rule to fallback model-eta-v2.0 for default and enterprise tiers. will push in 30s.

mike: notify customers on impacted endpoints — CS team queued a message template. some customers already reported timeouts.

ash: executing rollback command now: `infractl rollout cancel --model model-eta-v2.1 && infractl promote --model model-eta-v2.0 --target gpu-east-2`

dan: also applying proxy guard: set MAX_CTX_TOKENS=2048 for new sessions on gpu-east-2 to limit kv growth. runbook step: limit_new_sessions_context.

incident-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: rollback_initiated by ash at 03:16Z, proxy_cap_set by dan at 03:17Z.

mike: metrics: enqueue rate starting to drop 03:20Z. 10m error rate trending down. p95 latency improving.

sara: can we confirm queue drained and scale requests allowed? Autoscaler still blocked on quota but rollback reduced memory pressure so effective capacity freed.

dan: queue length now 230 -> 60 -> 12 over next 18m. p99 back to ~1.1s by 03:34Z. throttling reduced to baseline. no further scale requests needed.

julia: routing change applied for enterprise and default. traffic for rollout group re-routed to model-eta-v2.0 and model-eta-lite for lower tiers.

ash: handing back to sara for monitoring/comms. I'm staying on until postmortem.

sara: thanks. initiating post-incident comms: customer-impact doc + status page update. assigning follow-ups:
- owner=dan: root cause analysis on tokenizer change + model warmup pattern (due 48h)
- owner=julia: add rollout gating test for per-session mem increase (due 72h)
- owner: infra: alert autoscaler quota rejection earlier and add synthetic for warmup amplification (due 72h)

mike: CS will send impacted customer list + outreach.

julia: quick note — we should add a rollout flag to prevent canary warmups from hitting production pool (runbook change).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: recovery observed at 2026-03-15T03:34:00Z. incident duration ~22 minutes. Follow-ups added. :white_check_mark:

sara: closing the thread. thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:
